rows.title: Turns and downturns in aging drivers.
rows.reason: This paper directly addresses the use of in-vehicle sensors to measure driving behavior in older adults, which matches the reader's area of expertise.
rows.summary: Researchers studied 106 older adults' driving habits and found that those with greater cognitive decline were less likely to make left turns, which could be an early sign of cognitive decline.

rows.title: Intrinsic capacity and mortality in community-dwelling octogenarians: a network analysis from the ilSIRENTE study.
rows.reason: The study is about older adults and intrinsic capacity, but it does not involve technology or measurement of daily function.
rows.summary: This study used network analysis to examine the relationships between different aspects of intrinsic capacity (such as mobility, cognition, and sensory function) in older adults and found that mobility was a key factor in determining survival. The study also found that higher intrinsic capacity scores were associated with lower mortality. The study used routine home-based assessments to measure intrinsic capacity in a group of 319 community-dwelling adults aged 80 and older.

rows.title: Validation of socialbit as a smartwatch algorithm for social interaction detection in a clinical population.
rows.reason: The technology is a smartwatch-based algorithm, which is similar to the GPS-guided walking app mentioned in the reader's profile, but it's used for social interaction detection rather than measuring daily function or cognition.
rows.summary: Researchers developed a smartwatch algorithm called SocialBit that can detect social interactions in real-time, and tested it with 153 hospitalized stroke patients. The algorithm was accurate and worked well even in patients with language deficits. The study found that patients with more severe strokes had less social interaction.

rows.title: Requirements of health professionals and affected persons for an App-based dual-task training for hearing impaired older adults - a Delphi survey.
rows.reason: The paper discusses the development of a technology-based training program for older adults with hearing impairments, but it does not focus on the technical aspects of building or deploying such a system.
rows.summary: A Delphi survey of health professionals and hearing-impaired older adults identified key features and preferences for an app-based dual-task training program, including flexibility, ease of use, and sensory accommodation.

rows.title: AI-Powered Framework for Personalized Prescription of Physical Activity in Aging: Proposing PEPHA, a framework for Personalized Phenotyping for Aging.
rows.reason: The paper discusses the use of wearable data and AI to analyze physical activity and sedentary behavior in older adults, which is related to the reader's work on in-home sensor networks and GPS-guided walking apps, but focuses on a different outcome (cognitive functioning and mental health) and population (older adults with cognitive decline).
rows.summary: Researchers developed an AI framework called PEPHA to analyze wearable data and identify personalized patterns of physical activity and sedentary behavior associated with cognitive functioning and mental health in older adults. The framework uses machine learning to identify specific periods when behavior is most relevant to health outcomes. The study found that PEPHA can uncover individualized, time-specific behavioral patterns and may help inform future personalized interventions.

rows.title: Detection of depression risk among older adults using home-deployed socially assistive robots: a real-world study.
rows.reason: The paper is about using a robot to monitor older adults, which is similar to the reader's experience with in-home sensor networks and web-based cognitive assessments, but the focus is on depression rather than cognition or daily function.
rows.summary: A study used a robot called Hyodol to monitor older adults' behavior and detect depression risk, with promising results, but also some false positives.

rows.title: From wrist data to lifespan: elucidating inflammation-driven biological aging via activity rhythms captured by wearable devices.
rows.reason: The paper uses wearable devices to study activity rhythms in older adults, but the focus is on inflammation and aging rather than cognition or daily function.
rows.summary: Researchers used wearable devices to study how daily activity rhythms and physical activity affect inflammation and aging in over 62,000 adults, finding that regular activity and stable rhythms can help mitigate the effects of inflammation on aging and mortality.

rows.title: Eye movements powered by artificial intelligence identify asymptomatic carriers of familial Alzheimer's disease.
rows.reason: The paper uses a technology (eye-tracking) that is similar to the sensor networks and cognitive assessments in the reader's profile, but it's focused on a different population (Alzheimer's disease carriers) and outcome (detection of asymptomatic carriers).
rows.summary: Researchers used eye-tracking technology and machine learning to identify people who are carriers of a genetic mutation that increases their risk of developing Alzheimer's disease, even if they don't show any symptoms yet.

rows.title: Remote Online-Based Application of the Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome Scale.
rows.reason: The study focuses on remote administration of a cognitive assessment tool, similar to the web-based cognitive assessment platform mentioned in the reader's profile, but for a different population and outcome.
rows.summary: A study evaluated the suitability of a cognitive assessment tool for remote administration in patients with cerebellar disease, finding that remote testing was feasible and reliable, but not necessarily equivalent to in-person testing.

rows.title: Feasibility and Acceptability of a Remote Sleep-Dependent Memory Assessment in Older Adults With Cognitive Concerns: Pilot Cross-Sectional Study.
rows.reason: The paper describes a mobile app used with older adults to measure cognition, but the focus is on sleep-dependent memory consolidation rather than the specific platforms mentioned in the reader's profile.
rows.summary: A mobile app, Sleep Memories, was tested with older adults to assess sleep-dependent memory consolidation. The app was found to be feasible and acceptable, with 68 participants completing at least one test. User feedback was positive, but some technical difficulties were reported.

rows.title: Remote cognitive training for older adults using tablets: A pilot trial.
rows.reason: The paper describes a tablet-based system used with older adults to measure cognition, but the focus is on the intervention rather than the technology itself.
rows.summary: A pilot trial tested a tablet-based cognitive training program for older adults with cognitive impairment or dementia, finding improved cognitive function in those who used the tablet compared to those who used a TV interface.

rows.title: Videoconference-integrated, computer-assisted cognitive testing improves the remote assessment of processing speed and attention.
rows.reason: The paper discusses the use of videoconference-based assessments for cognitive testing, which is relevant to the reader's work on remote health data collection and cognitive assessment platforms, but focuses on a different population and outcome.
rows.summary: Researchers compared in-person and remote videoconference-based assessments of cognitive processing speed and attention using various versions of two standard tests. They found that a digital version of one test was as effective as the in-person version, while an oral version was less effective. The study suggests that videoconference-integrated digital tasks could be a useful tool for remote cognitive assessments.

rows.title: Effect of Multi-Modal Training in Patients With Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial.
rows.reason: The paper is about a cognitive training program for older adults, but it doesn't mention any specific technology or platform used to deliver the training.
rows.summary: A 24-week multi-modal training program improved cognitive function in older adults with mild cognitive impairment, compared to health education alone.

rows.title: Cognitive behavioural therapy for older adults with depressive symptoms living in residential aged care: A pilot study of a systemic treatment model.
rows.reason: The paper is about a therapy program for older adults, but it does not involve technology or measurement of cognition or daily function.
rows.summary: A pilot study tested a therapy program for older adults with depression in residential care, delivered by supervised students. The program included cognitive, behavioral, and reminiscence techniques, and showed promising results with high treatment satisfaction and small-to-medium effect sizes for reducing depression and anxiety.

rows.title: An exploratory descriptive qualitative study examining the experiences and perceptions of family caregivers engaging in structured home-based reminiscence activities with persons with dementia.
rows.reason: The study involves a reminiscence activity, which is related to the reader's work on a GPS-guided walking app for a social reminiscence intervention, but the focus is on caregivers and people with dementia rather than older adults in general.
rows.summary: A study of family caregivers in Singapore who used a structured reminiscence activity package to engage with people with dementia at home, finding it feasible and beneficial but needing personalization and cultural adaptation.

rows.title: Cortisol awakening response and autobiographical memory in healthy older adults: The moderating role of negative reminiscence.
rows.reason: The study mentions older adults and cognitive functioning, but the focus is on the psychological and physiological factors affecting autobiographical memory, rather than technology-based measurement or intervention.
rows.summary: This study found that older adults who experience high levels of stress and negative thoughts about their past are more likely to have less specific memories of their experiences.

rows.title: From digital companionship to capability building: reframing conversational artificial intelligence and older adults' psychological wellbeing in active aging.
rows.reason: The paper discusses conversational AI and its use with older adults, but the focus is on its potential to build capabilities, which is adjacent to the reader's work on using conversational AI for social engagement and isolation.
rows.summary: This paper argues that conversational AI can help older adults build capabilities, rather than just providing companionship, and proposes a framework to understand how this works.

rows.title: Addressing the silent epidemic: a narrative review and evidence synthesis of digital health and telehealth interventions for loneliness in older adults.
rows.reason: The paper discusses the use of digital health technologies with older adults, but focuses on loneliness rather than cognition or daily function, and does not specifically mention the types of platforms or systems described in the reader's profile.
rows.summary: A review of digital health and telehealth interventions for loneliness in older adults found that some approaches, such as video visits and AI-enabled social robots, show promise in reducing loneliness, but the effectiveness of these interventions varies and is influenced by design features and population characteristics.

rows.title: Social needs in home care for older adults: A qualitative exploration of recognition, expectations and opportunities.
rows.reason: The paper discusses the importance of social interaction in home care for older adults, which is related to the reader's work on technology platforms for social engagement and cognitive assessment, but focuses on qualitative exploration of perceptions and experiences rather than technology development or deployment.
rows.summary: A qualitative study found that older adults value companionship and small acts of kindness from home care staff, which are essential for their experience of care. Home care nurses and administrators have differing views on who should address social needs. The study suggests that social needs should be integrated into daily care interactions, not treated as separate tasks.

rows.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Digital Social Robots in Reducing Loneliness Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults in Japan: Randomized Controlled Trial and Qualitative Analysis.
rows.reason: The study uses a technology platform (digital social robot) with a similar population (older adults), but with a different focus (reducing loneliness) and outcome (well-being).
rows.summary: A study in Japan found that a digital social robot reduced loneliness and improved well-being in older adults living alone, and identified categories of benefits including emotional support and lifestyle assistance.

rows.title: Bridging language markers and pathology: correlations between digital speech measures and surrogate CSF biomarkers in Alzheimer's disease.
rows.reason: The paper is about using digital speech measures with older adults, but it's focused on Alzheimer's disease pathology rather than daily function or cognition in a broader sense.
rows.summary: A study found correlations between digital speech measures and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers in Alzheimer's disease, suggesting that conversational language could be used for early detection and monitoring.

rows.title: Bridging Language Markers and Pathology: Correlations Between Digital Speech Measures and Surrogate CSF Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease.
rows.reason: The paper discusses digital speech measures, but they are used with a different population (Alzheimer's patients) and outcome (disease detection) than the reader's platforms.
rows.summary: Researchers found correlations between digital speech measures and biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease, suggesting that conversational language could be used to detect and monitor the disease.

rows.title: Systemic sclerosis in 2026: emerging paradigms from the World Scleroderma Congress.
rows.reason: The paper is about a different disease and population, with no mention of technology or measurement of cognition or daily function in older adults.
rows.summary: The article discusses recent advances in understanding and treating systemic sclerosis, a chronic autoimmune disease, including new diagnostic methods and therapeutic strategies.

rows.title: Recent advances in tumor microenvironment-responsive pro-antibody to overcome on-target, off-tumor toxicity.
rows.reason: This paper is about a new type of antibody therapy, not related to technology platforms for aging research or measuring cognition and daily function in older adults.
rows.summary: Researchers have developed antibodies that only activate in the tumor microenvironment, reducing side effects. This review discusses the design and limitations of these antibodies. The goal is to create safer and more effective cancer treatments.

rows.title: uPAR-Targeting T Cell Engager Exerts Senolytic Effects in Mice and Non-Human Primates With Serum Aminotransferase Activity as a Safety Monitor.
rows.reason: This paper is about a new type of senolytic therapy, but it does not involve technology platforms for measuring cognition or daily function in older adults.
rows.summary: Researchers developed a new type of senolytic therapy that targets senescent cells in mice and primates without causing harm, using a low dose that can be monitored by liver enzyme levels.

rows.title: Oncofetal antigens as emerging targets in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell-based immunotherapies: opportunities and challenges.
rows.reason: This paper is about a type of immunotherapy, but it does not mention older adults or any technology related to the reader's profile.
rows.summary: Researchers are exploring the use of oncofetal antigens as targets for CAR-T cell therapies, which have shown promise in some cancers but face challenges in solid tumors.

rows.title: Oral Health Care Interventions by Functional Status Among Older Adults in a Nursing Home and Day Care Centre: A Pilot Study.
rows.reason: The paper is about older adults, but it focuses on oral health care rather than technology or cognitive function.
rows.summary: A pilot study found that tailored oral health care programs improved oral hygiene in older adults in nursing homes and day care centers, regardless of their functional status.

rows.title: Disparities in Dental Care Access, Oral Cancer Counseling, and Oral Cancer Examination Among U.S. Adults with a History of Cancer: Results from NHANES, 2015-2018.
rows.reason: The paper is about healthcare access and disparities, but does not mention technology or older adults.
rows.summary: This study found that US adults with a history of cancer were more likely to receive oral cancer counseling and exams, but still faced disparities in dental care access.

rows.title: Periodontitis, Edentulism, and Accelerated Biological Aging: A Population-Based Study of Epigenetic Clocks.
rows.reason: The paper is about a population-based study of aging, but it does not involve technology or measurement of cognition or daily function in older adults.
rows.summary: A study of 1,926 adults found that severe periodontitis and edentulism are linked to accelerated aging, as measured by epigenetic clocks.

rows.title: Frailty in Cardiorenal Care: A Geriatric Perspective on the 2026 European Society of Cardiology Guidelines.
rows.reason: The paper discusses the limitations of current guidelines for older adults and proposes a new framework, but it does not specifically address the technology platforms mentioned in the reader's profile.
rows.summary: The 2026 European Society of Cardiology Guidelines for cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease may not fully capture the needs of older adults, and a new framework called STAMP-F is proposed to incorporate frailty, function, and future healthspan into treatment decisions.
